ui.router_question: WHERE does the fold or pull sit?
ui.not_this_sign: None of these — the sign matched but no cause did. Chapter 8 says what to do (sign index: page {apx_c})
ui.fix_first: Fix this FIRST — do not touch the pattern
ui.all_clear: All ruled out — continue to diagnosis
ui.scale_note: Not to scale — proportions are schematic
ui.source_conflict: Sources differ — see the note beside this measurement.
ui.no_source: No published definition — this book's own, stated in Chapter 2.
ui.cross_route: If instead {cond}, that is {fam} — start from that region's entries.
ui.curve_on_edge: Tape standing on edge, walked along the seam line
ui.curve_flat: Tape lying flat — only for straight runs
ui.offset_read_front: Seen from the side; the front is to the right.

SYM-001.observation: The front neckline stands away from the chest, above the breastbone.

causes.cause: Neckline cut too wide or too deep for the body
causes.evidence: The gap is the same when you stand upright and when you lean forward, it is even all the way round, and the BACK neckline stands away as well.

causes.cause: Bust volume is pulling the neckline forward
causes.evidence: The gap GROWS clearly when you lean forward, it is at the FRONT only — the back neckline lies flat — and the front hem sits higher than the back. It is usually the same on both sides, not one-sided.

causes.cause: The neckline edge was stretched while sewing
causes.evidence: The gap looks wavy or slack rather than a clean opening.

SYM-002.observation: The neckline presses into the base of the neck, leaves a mark, or makes swallowing uncomfortable.

causes.cause: Neckline cut too tight for the body
causes.evidence: The pressure is even all the way around.

causes.cause: A rounded upper back is pushing the neck forward
causes.evidence: Pressure is clear at the BACK neckline and absent at the front; the back neckline also rides up.

causes.cause: The shoulder seam has shifted forward and is loading the neckline
causes.evidence: The shoulder seam sits BEHIND the top-of-shoulder line — the shoulder is carried forward and the seam has been left behind it — and it creeps forward as you wear it.

SYM-003.observation: The back neckline rides up and rubs the neck, and the back hem rises at the same time.

causes.cause: Back bodice length is too short overall
causes.evidence: The front hem hangs level; ONLY the back rises.

causes.cause: Not enough width across the shoulder blades, pulling the fabric up
causes.evidence: The rise comes with horizontal tension at shoulder-blade level.

causes.cause: The back neckline is too narrow and is hanging the garment up
causes.evidence: The neckline rises the most and the hem follows it only slightly; the back is clean between them.

SYM-004.observation: Diagonal drag lines run from the neck point down toward the underarm.

causes.cause: Shoulder slope is squarer than the pattern assumes
causes.evidence: Lines run OUT and DOWN from the neck point; fabric is tight at the shoulder tip and the seam is pressed onto the shoulder.

causes.cause: Shoulder slope is more sloping than the pattern assumes
causes.evidence: Lines run the other way — from the shoulder tip toward the neck; fabric GATHERS at the shoulder tip.

causes.cause: Shoulder width is too narrow
causes.evidence: Lines are present but the slope is right; the armhole seam sits INSIDE the shoulder tip.

SYM-005.observation: Fabric gathers into a horizontal fold just below the shoulder seam, near the armhole.

causes.cause: Shoulder slope drawn too square for a sloping-shouldered wearer
causes.evidence: The gathering is near the shoulder TIP and absent at the neck end.

causes.cause: Armhole cut too deep and the sleeve cap too high
causes.evidence: The fold follows the armhole and disappears when the arm is raised.

causes.cause: Shoulder width is too wide
causes.evidence: Along with the fold, the sleeve cap hangs OUTSIDE the shoulder tip.

SYM-006.observation: The shoulder seam sits BEHIND the top-of-shoulder line and keeps sliding forward.

causes.cause: Forward shoulder posture
causes.evidence: The seam sits back on BOTH shoulders, and it does so when you stand relaxed.

causes.cause: A rounded upper back is pulling fabric backward
causes.evidence: The seam is displaced BUT there is also horizontal tension at shoulder-blade level.

causes.cause: Front bodice is short relative to the back
causes.evidence: The front hem rises as well.

SYM-007.observation: The shoulder seam passes the shoulder tip and hangs onto the arm; the sleeve cap drops.

causes.cause: Shoulder width is too wide for this body
causes.evidence: The overhang is symmetrical on both shoulders; the armhole seam sits OUTSIDE the shoulder bone.

causes.cause: The design is a deliberate drop shoulder
causes.evidence: The pattern envelope or line drawing shows a dropped shoulder, and the armhole is deep as well.

causes.cause: Shoulder slope drawn too square
causes.evidence: The overhang comes with fabric gathering at the shoulder tip.

SYM-008.observation: Reaching forward produces a hard pull across the back; the garment restricts movement.

causes.cause: Not enough width across the back
causes.evidence: The sign is ABSENT with the arm at your side; it appears only when you reach forward.

causes.cause: Armhole too narrow or shifted forward
causes.evidence: The pull concentrates at the armhole edge, not at the centre of the back.

causes.cause: Not enough sleeve-cap ease, or the sleeve is narrow
causes.evidence: The pull is felt in the sleeve itself as well.

SYM-009.observation: A horizontal fold of excess fabric sits across the back at shoulder-blade level.

causes.cause: Back bodice length is too long
causes.evidence: The fold stays when the arm is raised; the neckline and shoulder sit correctly.

causes.cause: The shaping allowed for the shoulder blades is not being filled (flat back)
causes.evidence: The fold is CONCENTRATED at blade level and fades downward; the pattern has a shoulder dart or ease that this body does not fill.

causes.cause: The back neckline is too high and is pushing fabric down
causes.evidence: The fold sits directly under the neckline and the neckline binds.

SYM-010.observation: Loose vertical folds hang down the back between the armholes.

causes.cause: Too much width across the back
causes.evidence: The folds are vertical and symmetrical, and reaching forward takes them up completely — the width that is surplus at rest is exactly what the reach needs.

causes.cause: One size too large was chosen
causes.evidence: The same excess is present at the front, in the sleeve and at the waist.

causes.cause: Armhole cut too wide
causes.evidence: The excess is only near the armhole; the centre back is clean.

SYM-011.observation: The back hem rises noticeably; the garment climbs up at the back.

causes.cause: Back bodice length is too short over the shoulder blades (rounded back)
causes.evidence: The back neckline is pulled up with the hem and the pull runs UP the back rather than across it; blade level is not horizontally taut.

causes.cause: Hip or seat volume is pulling the fabric up
causes.evidence: The rise starts BELOW the waist; blade level is clean.

causes.cause: Front-to-back balance is off (forward-leaning posture)
causes.evidence: The front hem DROPS while the back rises — the two happen together.

SYM-012.observation: The centre-back seam or zipper does not hang straight; it bows outward.

causes.cause: Sway back — excess length at centre back at waist level
causes.evidence: The bow is strongest at waist level, with horizontal folds just above it.

causes.cause: Rounded back — not enough length at upper centre back
causes.evidence: The bow is at blade level and the fabric there is TAUT rather than loose — the seam is being pulled out, not falling out. The waist is clean.

causes.cause: The zipper was stretched while sewing
causes.evidence: The bow is irregular and wavy; the fabric is puckered along the zipper.

SYM-013.observation: With the arm down, the underarm binds and the garment is pulled up from the shoulder.

causes.cause: Armhole cut too shallow (underarm too high)
causes.evidence: Comfortable with the arm up, binding with the arm down; there is a red mark under the arm.

causes.cause: The sleeve is narrow at the bicep
causes.evidence: The binding is felt inside the sleeve; the armhole itself is comfortable.

causes.cause: Bust volume is pulling the front armhole up
causes.evidence: The binding is at the FRONT underarm, with drag lines running from the bust toward the armhole.

SYM-014.observation: The FRONT edge of the armhole stands away from the body above the bust.

causes.cause: Too much width across the front chest
causes.evidence: The gap is there with the arm at your side, and the upper chest feels slack.

causes.cause: The bust dart apex is off position, leaving excess above the bust
causes.evidence: Along with the gap there is a hollow, empty area ABOVE the bust.

causes.cause: Shoulder width is too wide
causes.evidence: The sleeve cap also hangs off the shoulder tip.

SYM-015.observation: The BACK edge of the armhole stands away from the body.

causes.cause: Too much width across the back
causes.evidence: There are loose vertical folds down the back as well.

causes.cause: Shoulder slope drawn too square
causes.evidence: There is fabric gathering at the shoulder tip as well.

causes.cause: Armhole drawn too wide
causes.evidence: The gap is even all the way around the armhole.

SYM-016.observation: Drag lines run from the bust point out toward the side seam or the armhole; the fabric is strained over the bust.

causes.cause: More bust volume than the pattern assumes
causes.evidence: The lines RADIATE from the bust point; the front hem also rides up and the front neckline gapes.

causes.cause: The whole front is too small (size choice)
causes.evidence: The same tightness is everywhere — waist, hip and sleeve — not only at the bust.

causes.cause: The dart point stops far from the apex, putting the volume in the wrong place
causes.evidence: There is tension BUT total front width is adequate; the dart point ends noticeably short of the apex.

SYM-017.observation: The front hem sits noticeably higher than the back hem; the garment looks short at the front.

causes.cause: Bust volume is pulling the front fabric up
causes.evidence: There are drag lines radiating from the bust as well, and the side seam swings forward.

causes.cause: Front bodice length is too short
causes.evidence: There are NO drag lines — only the length is short, and the bust area is comfortable.

causes.cause: Abdominal volume is pulling the fabric up
causes.evidence: The rise starts BELOW the waist; the bust is clean.

SYM-018.observation: The side seams do not hang vertically; they swing toward the front.

causes.cause: Not enough volume in the front at bust level
causes.evidence: The swing comes with tightness across the bust.

causes.cause: Too much width across the back
causes.evidence: The seam swings but there is NO tightness at the front; the back has loose vertical folds.

causes.cause: The fabric was cut off grain
causes.evidence: One side swings and the other does not, and the grainline on that piece is not parallel to the selvedge.

SYM-019.observation: The fabric puckers or forms a small bubble at the point of the bust dart.

causes.cause: The dart point ends on top of the apex (dart too long)
causes.evidence: The bubble is exactly at the dart point; the apex itself is flat.

causes.cause: The dart takes up more volume than this body needs
causes.evidence: There is general slackness around the dart as well.

causes.cause: The dart was not tapered to nothing when sewn
causes.evidence: The pucker is irregular; there is a knot or backstitch at the dart point.

SYM-020.observation: There is a hollow, collapsing area ABOVE the bust, between the collarbone and the bust.

causes.cause: The bust dart is positioned above the apex
causes.evidence: The hollow is directly above the dart, and the dart point sits above the apex.

causes.cause: Too much width across the upper front
causes.evidence: The hollow is spread over a wide area, and the front edge of the armhole gapes as well.

causes.cause: The pattern was drafted for a fuller upper chest
causes.evidence: The hollow follows the high-bust line, and your high bust is smaller than the pattern assumes.

SYM-021.observation: The button band pulls open horizontally at bust level; gaps appear between the buttons.

causes.cause: Not enough bust volume
causes.evidence: The opening is CONCENTRATED at bust level; the closure lies flat above and below.

causes.cause: The front extension is too narrow
causes.evidence: The opening is spread EVENLY along the whole closure.

causes.cause: There is no button at bust level
causes.evidence: The gap falls between two buttons, and there is no button at apex height.

SYM-022.observation: The waist seam or waistband sits above or below your natural waist.

causes.cause: Bodice length differs from what the pattern assumes
causes.evidence: The displacement is EVEN all the way around — the same amount front and back.

causes.cause: Front-to-back balance is off
causes.evidence: The displacement is a DIFFERENT amount at the front and at the back.

causes.cause: The design is deliberately high- or low-waisted
causes.evidence: The pattern line drawing and the finished-garment measurements show this.

SYM-023.observation: Fabric pools in horizontal folds just ABOVE the waist at the back.

causes.cause: Sway back — excess length at centre back at waist level
causes.evidence: The excess is concentrated at CENTRE BACK and fades toward the side seams; the front is clean.

causes.cause: Back bodice length is too long overall
causes.evidence: The excess is spread EVENLY across the back width, including at the side seams.

causes.cause: Seat volume is pushing the fabric up
causes.evidence: The pooling comes with horizontal drag lines over the seat.

SYM-024.observation: The waistband stands away from the body at the back, leaving a gap.

causes.cause: Sway back
causes.evidence: The gap is widest at centre back and closes at the sides; there is pooling just above the waist as well.

causes.cause: Your waist-to-hip ratio differs from the pattern's
causes.evidence: The waistband fits the waist, but the hip area is tight or loose.

causes.cause: The waistband was cut too long
causes.evidence: The gap is as large at the sides as at the back, and the band is loose all the way round rather than standing away only behind you.

SYM-025.observation: Loose vertical folds sit at waist level near the side seams.

causes.cause: Too much waist circumference
causes.evidence: The folds are vertical and symmetrical; the bust and hip fit.

causes.cause: Not enough waist shaping (darts)
causes.evidence: The folds sit close to the side seams and the waist measures adequate against the pattern, but the pattern has no waist dart — or only a shallow one — where your own hip-minus-waist difference says shaping is needed.

causes.cause: One size too large was chosen
causes.evidence: The same excess is present at the bust and hip.

SYM-026.observation: The waist seam or waistband binds; it is uncomfortable when you sit and leaves a mark.

causes.cause: Not enough waist circumference
causes.evidence: The binding is even all the way around and increases when you sit.

causes.cause: The waistline sits at the wrong level (below the natural waist)
causes.evidence: The binding is below the waist, at abdomen level.

causes.cause: Abdominal volume
causes.evidence: The binding is at the FRONT only; the back is comfortable.

SYM-027.observation: Horizontal drag lines cross the seat; the fabric is strained over it.

causes.cause: More seat volume than the pattern assumes
causes.evidence: The lines are CONCENTRATED over the seat; the side seam swings back and the back hem rises.

causes.cause: Not enough crotch length (in trousers)
causes.evidence: Along with the lines, the crotch is pulled up and sitting down is difficult.

causes.cause: Not enough hip circumference overall
causes.evidence: The same tightness is present at the FRONT too, and your bust and waist fall in the same size as your hip does — so it is the whole size, not the seat.

SYM-028.observation: Fabric sags just BELOW the seat, forming an empty pouch.

causes.cause: Less seat volume than the pattern assumes (flat seat)
causes.evidence: The sag is below the seat; there is NO tension over the seat.

causes.cause: Crotch length is too long
causes.evidence: The sag reaches down into the crotch area, and the crotch does not touch the body.

causes.cause: Back bodice or skirt length is too long
causes.evidence: The sag is a horizontal fold and reaches up to waist level.

SYM-029.observation: The skirt or trouser rides up over one hip; the hem is not parallel to the floor.

causes.cause: Body asymmetry (one hip higher or fuller)
causes.evidence: The rise is on ONE SIDE and persists when you distribute your weight evenly.

causes.cause: Posture: weight resting on one leg
causes.evidence: The rise DISAPPEARS when you even out your weight.

causes.cause: The fabric was cut off grain
causes.evidence: The rise comes with the side seam spiralling.

SYM-030.observation: The side seam swings toward the back at hip level.

causes.cause: Not enough volume at the back
causes.evidence: The swing comes with horizontal tension over the seat.

causes.cause: Too much volume at the front
causes.evidence: The seam swings but there is NO tension at the back; the front is slack.

causes.cause: The fabric was cut off grain
causes.evidence: The swing is on one side only.

SYM-031.observation: Diagonal drag lines run from the sleeve cap toward the bicep and increase when the arm is raised.

causes.cause: Not enough width at the bicep
causes.evidence: The lines concentrate at the bicep line and increase clearly when the arm is raised.

causes.cause: The sleeve cap is too high
causes.evidence: The lines are around the cap; the bicep is comfortable.

causes.cause: The armhole is narrow and is pinching the sleeve
causes.evidence: The lines start at the armhole seam; the sleeve alone is comfortable.

SYM-032.observation: Loose vertical folds hang in the upper sleeve; the sleeve looks baggy.

causes.cause: Too much sleeve width
causes.evidence: The folds are vertical and arm movement is completely free.

causes.cause: The design is deliberately a full sleeve
causes.evidence: The pattern line drawing and finished-measurement table show a full sleeve.

causes.cause: Too much sleeve-cap ease, gathering at the cap
causes.evidence: The excess concentrates at the cap and fades downward.

SYM-033.observation: The sleeve twists on the arm; the underarm seam spirals instead of hanging straight.

causes.cause: Sleeve-cap notches are misaligned (shifted front or back)
causes.evidence: The twist runs the SAME way on both sleeves, and the cap notches do not line up with the shoulder seam.

causes.cause: The sleeve's elbow curve does not match the arm's carriage (forward arm)
causes.evidence: The twist shows with the arm hanging relaxed, and there is a pull at elbow level.

causes.cause: The sleeve was cut off grain
causes.evidence: The twist is on ONE sleeve only.

SYM-034.observation: The sleeve cap puckers where it joins the armhole.

causes.cause: Too much cap ease for this fabric
causes.evidence: The puckering is along the upper curve of the cap, and the fabric is crisp or firm.

causes.cause: The ease is right but it was not distributed before setting the sleeve
causes.evidence: The puckering is irregular and bunched, with tucks at particular points.

causes.cause: The armhole was sewn to a different measurement than the pattern
causes.evidence: The puckering is even all the way round rather than concentrated at the top of the cap, and the seam allowance actually used is not the one the pattern specifies.

SYM-035.observation: Horizontal drag lines sit under the seat; the crotch is pulled up and is uncomfortable.

causes.cause: Not enough crotch depth
causes.evidence: It increases clearly when you sit and eases when you stand.

causes.cause: Not enough back crotch length
causes.evidence: It is present standing as well, and the seat is under tension too.

causes.cause: The back crotch curve is too straight for this body
causes.evidence: Crotch depth and back crotch length have both been measured against the pattern and both are adequate, and the pull is confined to the bend of the curve rather than spread across the seat.

SYM-036.observation: Fabric collects in a U-shape at the front crotch.

causes.cause: Front crotch length is too long
causes.evidence: The excess is at the front crotch; the back is clean.

causes.cause: Crotch depth is too deep
causes.evidence: The excess is at both front and back, and the crotch does not touch the body.

causes.cause: The front crotch curve is scooped too deeply
causes.evidence: Front crotch length and crotch depth have both been measured against the pattern and both are adequate, and the pooling is confined to the curve of the seam rather than spread across the front.

SYM-037.observation: Diagonal drag lines run from the crotch point toward the hip.

causes.cause: Not enough thigh circumference
causes.evidence: The lines concentrate at thigh level and increase when you sit.

causes.cause: The crotch curve does not match the body
causes.evidence: The lines come straight off the crotch point; thigh circumference is adequate.

causes.cause: Abdominal or seat volume is pulling the fabric toward the crotch
causes.evidence: The lines run downward, starting at abdomen or seat level.

SYM-038.observation: The trouser leg twists; the inseam does not hang straight.

causes.cause: Leg carriage (knees turning in or out) is rotating the fabric
causes.evidence: The twist is symmetrical on both legs and shows when standing.

causes.cause: The crotch curve is unbalanced front to back
causes.evidence: The twist starts at crotch level.

causes.cause: The leg was cut off grain
causes.evidence: The twist is on ONE leg only.

SYM-039.observation: The crotch hangs low and away from the body, making it hard to take a step.

causes.cause: Crotch depth is too deep
causes.evidence: The gap between crotch and body is there standing as well, and sitting is comfortable.

causes.cause: The design has a deliberately dropped crotch
causes.evidence: The pattern line drawing shows a low crotch.

causes.cause: The waistline sits below the natural waist
causes.evidence: The waistband sits low and the crotch has come down with it.

SYM-040.observation: The hem is not parallel to the floor; it rises or drops in one area.

causes.cause: A volume is pulling the fabric up
causes.evidence: The rise is on the side of that volume, and there are drag lines in the same area.

causes.cause: Front-to-back balance is off
causes.evidence: One side rises while the other drops; it is symmetrical.

causes.cause: Body asymmetry
causes.evidence: The rise is on one side and persists when your weight is evened out.

SYM-041.observation: The garment rotates on the body; the side seams migrate forward or backward as you wear it.

causes.cause: Front-to-back volume distribution does not match the body
causes.evidence: The rotation runs consistently in one direction and repeats every time you wear it.

causes.cause: Body asymmetry
causes.evidence: The rotation is one-directional and comes with other one-sided signs.

causes.cause: The pieces were cut off grain
causes.evidence: The rotation is irregular; the grainlines are not parallel to the selvedge.

SYM-042.observation: The centre front or centre back does not hang perpendicular to the floor; the balance lines are not level.

causes.cause: Posture (leaning forward or back) is throwing the balance off
causes.evidence: The deviation is symmetrical and persists in your natural standing posture.

causes.cause: A volume (bust or seat) is pulling the fabric
causes.evidence: The deviation starts at the level of that volume.

causes.cause: A piece was cut off grain
causes.evidence: The deviation is in one piece only and is irregular.

SYM-043.observation: A LENGTH is wrong (sleeve, leg, hem or bodice) but there is no other sign at all: no wrinkles, no drag, no displacement, no gaping.

causes.cause: The pattern's length does not match your height
causes.evidence: The garment sits cleanly everywhere, the balance lines are true, and there is no drag or fold — ONLY the length differs.

causes.cause: The design is deliberately short or long
causes.evidence: The pattern line drawing and finished-measurement table show this length.

causes.cause: The hem allowance was turned differently than the pattern assumes
causes.evidence: The difference equals the pattern's hem allowance; the rest of the garment matches the pattern exactly.

horizontal_fold: Fabric standing in a fold across the body — excess LENGTH, the dimension at right angles to the fold
vertical_fold: Fabric standing in a fold up and down — excess WIDTH, the dimension at right angles to the fold
diagonal_drag_line: Fabric pulled into diagonal lines — a shortage, and the lines point toward it
gape: An edge standing away from the body with nothing holding it
strain_pull: Fabric under tension: it binds, marks the skin, or restricts movement
pooling: Fabric collecting and sagging where it is not supported
hem_hike: A hem no longer parallel to the floor — almost always a consequence
seam_displacement: A seam not where it was drawn to be — an indicator, rarely a cause
grain_distortion: Lengthwise or crosswise grain no longer square to the floor
silhouette_deviation: The garment's outline differs from the one the design drew
